section.name: EBApplicability20261008
section.heading: Pile section applicability
section.paragraph: The pipe section formulas below apply to the pier’s 20-in pipe piles. Both end bents use the current 18-in square pile envelope recorded in Bridge Geometry. Do not apply these pipe thickness, steel area, stiffness or corrosion allowances to the end-bent piles; their material, reinforcement, section properties and foundation checks require the applicable pile design/model.

paragraph.link: Current end-bent design and coherence record

report.heading: Sacrificial Thickness
report.paragraph: Steel thickness set aside as the sacrificial-loss allowance.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_034_Sacrificial_thk
section.paragraph: This input records the thickness allowance to leave out of the structural section when representing the adopted section-loss condition. The next expression subtracts an explicitly entered allowance; it does not refer to this variable by name.

report.paragraph: Steel wall thickness left after subtracting the entered allowance.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_035_Pile_modelThickness
section.paragraph: Start with the full 5/8 in pipe wall and subtract the fixed 0.15 in sacrificial allowance shown in this equation. The remainder is the wall thickness represented for this model note. “To in” displays it in inches.
The effective thickness used in the pipe-property section is entered separately, so changing this result alone does not automatically change all of those properties.

report.heading: Pile section data
report.paragraph: PIPE PILE SECTION PROPERTIES — USE THE LIVE DIMENSIONS BELOW
Outside diameter of the circular pipe pile used by these section equations.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_036_D_o
section.paragraph: This is the full diameter across the outer surface of the pipe. The following equations use this live input for the actual and reduced steel sections. The model keeps this outside diameter fixed when it represents the thinner effective wall.

report.paragraph: Full as-built pipe wall thickness before the adopted section loss.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_037_t_actual
section.paragraph: This is the thickness of steel on one side of the original pipe wall. It defines the actual steel area and the weight that the model is intended to retain.

report.paragraph: Reduced wall thickness used for stiffness and section properties.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_038_t_eff
section.paragraph: This is the effective steel thickness remaining in the adopted section-loss model. It defines the reduced steel area, bending properties, and torsional property. It is an independent input here, rather than a live subtraction from the actual thickness.

report.paragraph: Inside diameter corresponding to the full as-built steel wall.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_039_D_i_actual
section.paragraph:
D_o
is the outside diameter. Subtract twice
t_actual
because a line across the pipe passes through a wall on one side and a wall on the opposite side. The distance left between the two inner wall faces is the inside diameter.

report.paragraph: Inside diameter corresponding to the reduced effective steel wall.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_040_D_i_eff
section.paragraph:
D_o
is the outside diameter. Subtract twice
t_eff
because a line across the pipe passes through a wall on one side and a wall on the opposite side. The distance left between the two inner wall faces is the inside diameter.

report.paragraph: Full circular footprint inside the pipe’s outside boundary.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_041_A_enclosed
section.paragraph:
Square
D_o
, the outside diameter, and multiply by pi divided by 4 to calculate the area of the entire outer circle. This includes the hollow interior as part of the footprint. It is not the amount of steel in the wall; the steel-ring areas below subtract the inside circle.

report.paragraph: Full enclosed pipe footprint expressed in square feet.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_042_A_enclosed_to_ft_2
section.paragraph:
Display
A_enclosed
, the full circular footprint including the hollow interior, in square feet. This converts area units only; it does not subtract the hollow area or change the geometry.

report.paragraph: Cross-sectional area of steel in the full as-built pipe ring.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_043_A_actual
section.paragraph:
D_o
is the outside diameter and
D_i_actual
is the inside diameter for this wall condition. Square each diameter, subtract the inner square from the outer square, then multiply by pi divided by 4.

Pi times diameter squared divided by 4 is the area of a solid circle. Subtracting the inner circle removes the hollow opening and leaves only the steel ring. The result is area, not the full enclosed footprint.

report.paragraph: Cross-sectional area of steel in the reduced effective pipe ring.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_044_A_eff
section.paragraph:
D_o
is the outside diameter and
D_i_eff
is the inside diameter for this wall condition. Square each diameter, subtract the inner square from the outer square, then multiply by pi divided by 4.

Pi times diameter squared divided by 4 is the area of a solid circle. Subtracting the inner circle removes the hollow opening and leaves only the steel ring. The result is area, not the full enclosed footprint.

report.paragraph: Second moment of area of the reduced pipe wall about a centroidal bending axis.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_045_I_x
section.paragraph:
Raise
D_o
, the outside diameter, and
D_i_eff
, the effective inside diameter, to the fourth power. Subtract the inner term from the outer term and multiply by pi divided by 64. This is the outer circle’s bending property minus the hollow opening’s bending property.

The result measures how the remaining steel is distributed away from the bending axis, with units of length to the fourth power. A larger value gives less bending curvature for the same moment and elastic modulus.

report.paragraph: Bending second moment of area about the perpendicular centroidal axis.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_046_I_y
section.paragraph:
Set it equal to
I_x
. A circular pipe ring looks the same when rotated 90° about its center, so the two centroidal bending axes have the same second moment of area in this section model.

report.paragraph: Elastic section modulus for bending of the reduced pipe wall.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_047_S_x
section.paragraph:
I_x
is the bending second moment of area. Divide it by half of
D_o
, which is the distance from the section center to the outside steel surface.
This packages the section geometry into the quantity used in elastic bending stress: moment divided by section modulus gives the extreme-fiber bending stress. Its units are length cubed.

report.paragraph: Elastic section modulus about the other centroidal bending axis.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_048_S_y
section.paragraph:
Use
S_x
because the circular section has the same geometry about both centroidal axes. This copies a section property; it does not copy a bending moment or a stress.

report.paragraph: Plastic section modulus of the reduced circular steel ring.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_049_Z_x
section.paragraph:
Cube
D_o
, the outside diameter, and
D_i_eff
, the effective inside diameter. Subtract the inner cube from the outer cube, then divide by 6. This sums the areas of the ring according to their distances from the plastic neutral axis.

The result describes the geometry used in a fully yielded plastic bending idealization. It is a section property with length-cubed units; this equation alone is not a strength or local-buckling check.

report.paragraph: Plastic section modulus about the other centroidal bending axis.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_050_Z_y
section.paragraph:
Set it equal to
Z_x
because the circular steel ring has the same section shape about both centroidal axes.

report.paragraph: Radius of gyration for the reduced steel area about the x axis.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_051_r_x
section.paragraph:
Divide
I_x
, the bending second moment of area, by
A_eff
, the effective steel area. The ratio has units of length squared. Sqrt takes its square root, leaving a length.
This length describes how far the steel area is spread from the axis in a stiffness sense. It is used in slenderness calculations; it is not the outside pipe radius.

report.paragraph: Radius of gyration about the other centroidal axis.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_052_r_y
section.paragraph:
Use
r_x
because the circular ring has the same area distribution about the two centroidal axes.

report.paragraph: Polar second moment of area for torsion of the reduced circular pipe ring.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_053_J
section.paragraph:
Raise
D_o
and
D_i_eff
to the fourth power, subtract the inner term from the outer term, and multiply by pi divided by 32. The subtraction removes the hollow part from the outer circular property.
For this circular tube, the result is the geometric torsional constant used with the shear modulus to describe resistance to twisting. It has units of length to the fourth power.

report.paragraph: Weight of one cubic foot of the original steel.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_054_gamma_steel
section.paragraph: This unit-weight input converts a volume of steel to a weight force. It is used with the actual steel area to preserve the pile’s original weight when the structural section is modeled with a reduced thickness.

report.paragraph: Adjusted model unit weight that preserves the full-thickness pile weight.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_055_gamma_steel_mod
section.paragraph:
gamma_steel
is the ordinary steel unit weight.
A_actual
is the steel area before the adopted loss, and
A_eff
is the smaller area used for structural properties. Multiply the ordinary unit weight by actual area divided by effective area.

This makes each modeled unit of reduced area carry more weight, so reduced area times adjusted unit weight equals actual area times ordinary unit weight. The adjustment is for model weight; it does not restore the lost stiffness or steel strength area.

report.paragraph: Pile weight per unit length using the reduced area and adjusted unit weight.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_056_w_pile
section.paragraph:
Multiply
A_eff
, the effective steel area, by
gamma_steel_mod
, the adjusted weight per volume. Area times weight per volume gives weight per length.

The explicit 12 in/ft term equals one physically and writes out the inch-to-foot conversion used in this expression. It does not represent twelve piles or additional steel. This combination is intended to retain the weight of the original full-thickness pipe.
